thread:
Priya Rao: Quick sync — need a decision on reserve-pool sizing vs burst credits for Q3 pilots (AcmePay + Lighthouse). They want predictable latency during surges and lower baseline cost. Options: increase committed headroom, soft-spill + prewarm addon, or predictive prewarm + opportunistic spill. Thoughts?
Jon Kim: Do we have real burst shape data? p95/p99, ramp rates?
Priya Rao: Sam shared roughs: AcmePay spikes ~3x for 20–90s; Lighthouse has long tails. Target from CS: p99 < 800ms for text-gen on dedicated lanes.
Maya Patel: 800ms p99 is plausible if KV cache hit > ~60% and batching stays consistent. Prewarm increases steady-state VRAM cost.
Sam Ortiz: AcmePay indicated willingness to pay for reserved carryover if it guarantees latency. Also asked for self-serve visibility into burst credits.
Linda Chow: Back-of-envelope: +20% committed headroom ≈ $18k/mo for pilot region; prewarm addon (on-demand) ≈ $6k/mo if infrequent. Quantify further after sims.
Jon Kim: Core tradeoff: committed headroom = simpler runtime & predictable latency but higher fixed cost. Soft-spill + prewarm = cheaper baseline, more complex ops (hysteresis, fallback).
Maya Patel: Quick runtime note — prewarm + keepalive avoids cold startups but has runaway cost if idle. Predictive prewarm needs short-term workload forecasting.
Jon Kim: We should also consider fallback to a smaller quantized model variant for best-effort workloads during overload. That reduces latency violations without extra reserved GPUs.
Priya Rao: Proposed minimal launch criteria: 1) telemetry for burst detection + simulation harness; 2) cost model comparing commit vs addon; 3) SLA draft for pilots; 4) dashboard for burst-credit visibility. Agree?
Sam Ortiz: +1. Also recommend pilot be opt-in with a clear rollback for customers if it hurts unit economics. AcmePay ok with pilot carveout.
Linda Chow: Finance preference: start with pay-as-you-go addons to validate demand, then migrate to committed offers if usage justifies.
Maya Patel: Suggested autoscale policy to prototype in staging:
```
{"policy":"predictive","scale_up_threshold":0.75,"scale_down_threshold":0.35,"min_replicas":2,"max_replicas":10,"cooldown_secs":180}
```
Jon Kim: That looks reasonable. Need to run sims with real spike traces and prewarm lead times (GPU spin-up + model load).
Priya Rao: Also: what about burst-credit accounting semantics? Should credits be per-tenant pool, pooled across orgs, or carryover month-to-month? CS preference is per-tenant with limited carryover.
Sam Ortiz: Per-tenant with small carryover window (e.g., 48h or a capped % per month) is what customers expect. Keeps billing simple.
Linda Chow: Carryover increases finance complexity — cap carryover at a low % to limit exposure.
Maya Patel: Ops risk: if we grant carryover plus low autoscale time constants, hot tenants could starve shared capacity. Need admission control + graceful degradation ordering.
Jon Kim: Action items: eng-platform run latency vs cost sims (owner: Jon), runtime prototype predictive autoscale + prewarm logic (owner: Maya), product draft pilot SLA + credit UX (owner: Priya), finance to model pricing ops (owner: Linda). Sam to coordinate pilot communication with AcmePay.
Priya Rao: I'll schedule a 30m follow-up Thu to review sims and the SLA draft. @deploy-bot please create the follow-up ticket.
deploy-bot: Created #ticket-6123: "reserved-pool-burn-rate-hedging: sims + prototype + pilot terms" :ticket: 
Priya Rao: Thanks all — bring sims, config tests, and a draft SLA to Thu. :thumbsup:
